scope: SQLite official compile.html, loadext.html, howtocompile.html and the SQLite Encryption Extension documentation

claims.claim: Feature trimming is done with real compile-time options such as SQLITE_OMIT_JSON, SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM, SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION, SQLITE_OMIT_DEPRECATED, SQLITE_OMIT_UTF16, SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE, SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT and SQLITE_OMIT_COMPLETE; optional modules are added with SQLITE_ENABLE_* (e.g. SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3/FTS5, SQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE)
claims.notes: Corrects the earlier chapter's non-existent SQLITE_OMIT_FTS4/FTS5 and SQLITE_OMIT_RTREE

claims.claim: SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM removes the VACUUM command; executing VACUUM then causes a parse error
Omitting deprecated interfaces (SQLITE_OMIT_DEPRECATED) does not make SQLite run faster but reduces the library footprint

An extension is a shared library/DLL or statically linked code; its entry point is sqlite3_extension_init, it uses SQLITE_EXTENSION_INIT1/INIT2, and registers capabilities with APIs such as sqlite3_create_function and sqlite3_create_module; when statically linking, rename the entry point to avoid collisions
The official encryption product is the SQLite Encryption Extension (SEE), whose source is provided only to licensees
claims.notes: The earlier chapter's home-rolled AES-256-ECB extension and invented size/optimization tables were removed

claims.claim: Loading extensions at run time is a security-sensitive operation and must be explicitly enabled by the application
claims.notes: Mechanistic guidance; exact enable/disable APIs are version-scoped

claims.claim: Compile-time options on an amalgamation build are set via preprocessor defines, and any trimming should be followed by re-running the test suite on the target platform
claims.notes: No size or speedup numbers are asserted; the earlier chapter's tables were unverifiable

claims.claim: Link-time and profile-guided compiler optimizations are applied by the compiler toolchain, not by SQLite itself, and their effect depends on the workload and platform
